title: Appointments, Not Just Leads — What Sales Teams Actually Need
content:
###  **Two Words That Get Used Interchangeably** 

A lead is a name and a phone number attached to some level of interest. An appointment is a homeowner who has agreed to a specific time. 

The gap between those two things is where most field marketing programs quietly fail. 

###  **Why Volume Alone Is Misleading** 

A program that produces a hundred leads and twelve appointments is not outperforming a program that produces thirty leads and eighteen appointments — even though the first number looks better in a report. 

Sales teams do not work leads. They work calendars. 

###  **Where the Drop-Off Happens** 

Some of it is lead quality. But a large share is what happens after — how quickly the company follows up, whether there is a process for homeowners who are interested but not ready, and whether anyone circles back when the timing improves. 

A lead that goes uncontacted for four days is usually gone. Not because the interest was fake, but because someone else called first. 

###  **What We Focus On** 

Our field conversations are structured toward a specific outcome — a homeowner who is genuinely open to a scheduled visit, not simply one who did not close the door. That produces fewer names on a list and more entries on a calendar.
